title: Four guidelines
metaphor: Building an idea in someone's mind is like building a bridge from their bank of the river: you start where they stand, not where you do.
hook: Once you accept that your job is to build an idea in the audience, four practical rules follow.
why_care: You can use these four rules as a checklist when you review your own draft.

screens.heading: Limit your focus, then make them curious

items.title: One idea only
items.text: Cut the content back to the single idea you care about most, so you can give context and examples.

items.title: Make it the through-line
items.text: Everything you say should link back to that one idea.

items.title: Stir curiosity
items.text: Ask intriguing questions that reveal a gap in the listener's [[worldview]] so they want it closed.

blocks.text: slash back your content so that you can focus on the single idea
blocks.speaker: Chris Anderson
blocks.meaning: A talk with five ideas leaves no room to explain any of them properly; pick one and give it room.

screens.heading: Use familiar concepts, make it worth sharing

blocks.text: Build the idea from concepts your audience already knows, in their language, not yours. A [[metaphor]] shows the shape of the pattern: CRISPR was explained as a word processor for DNA. Then test the talk on trusted friends to find what confuses them.

blocks.title: The honesty test
blocks.text: Ask who the idea benefits and answer honestly. If it only serves you or your organisation, the speaker says it is probably not worth sharing.

blocks.title: Checklist for a draft
blocks.caption: The four guidelines as a loop you can repeat while rewriting.

quiz.question: Your draft explains a technical term with another technical term the audience has not met. Which guideline does this break, and what is the fix?
options: Limit your focus: delete the term
Use familiar concepts: explain it with something they already know, such as a metaphor
Make it valuable: ask who it benefits
quiz.explain_right: The third guideline builds the idea from concepts already in the listeners' minds, and metaphors show the shape of the pattern.
quiz.explain_wrong: The other guidelines are about scope, curiosity and benefit, not about unfamiliar vocabulary.

glossary.definition: The structure of linked ideas in a person's mind that they use to make sense of the world.
Explaining something new by comparing it to something the listener already understands.
The single idea that runs through a whole talk so that everything links back to it.

key_takeaways: Limit the talk to one major idea and make it the through-line.
Stir curiosity before you start building.
Build from concepts the audience already knows and ask who the idea benefits.
